runs.summary: IREN’s central thesis is a transition from Bitcoin mining toward a vertically integrated AI cloud business. FY2026 revenue grew, but Bitcoin mining remained the larger segment; substantial losses and capital spending leave the transition dependent on delivery, revenue conversion, and improving economics. August’s reported contracted ARR and GPU financing support the expansion case, while the gap between operating capacity and broader power arrangements underscores execution uncertainty.

keyFindings.text: Observed fact: For the year ended June 30, 2026, IREN reported $707.0 million in revenue: $128.8 million from AI Cloud Services and $578.2 million from Bitcoin mining. AI accounted for 18.2% of reported revenue.

Issuer claim: IREN’s August 27 results announcement reported $4 billion of contracted ARR for 2026 capacity, $1 billion operating at that time, and 2026 capacity largely sold out. These annualized run rates are distinct from FY2026 recognized revenue.

Observed fact: As of June 30, 2026, IREN reported about 40 MW of operating AI computing capacity and about 5 GW of power agreements or similar arrangements, plus a further multi-gigawatt development pipeline. The evidence does not establish how quickly those arrangements can become energized, equipped, and utilized capacity.

Observed fact: FY2026 revenue grew 41.1% year over year, while operating income was negative $1.05 billion, net income attributable to the parent was negative $702.6 million, and diluted EPS was negative $2.22. Capex was $3.00 billion; the supplied free-cash-flow proxy was negative $897.6 million.

Observed fact: At June 30, 2026, cash was $5.90 billion and debt was $7.59 billion, for net debt of $1.70 billion. IREN reported $2.8 billion of GPU financing covering 90% of associated GPU capex; that figure does not establish coverage of all infrastructure or future funding needs.

risks.text: Execution and monetization risk: the company-reported contracted ARR materially exceeds operating ARR, while reported AI revenue remained a minority of FY2026 revenue. The evidence does not provide detailed contract commencement schedules or deployment milestones.

Funding and dilution risk: debt exceeded cash at the latest reported period, FY2026 capex was substantial, and diluted shares increased 41.6% year over year. The supplied evidence does not establish a complete forward funding plan.
Customer concentration and contract-quality risk remain difficult to assess because customer-level revenue shares, commencement schedules, renewal rates, and repeat-purchase rates are not supplied.

Valuation sensitivity is elevated in the supplied evidence: IREN trades at 25.33x EV to annualized FY2026 revenue, above the reported 11.22x peer median, but that median is based on one core peer and multiple peers were excluded.
Observed fact: The latest supplied reported financial period ended June 30, 2026. This limits visibility into subsequent deployment, liquidity, leverage, and operating results.

catalysts.text: Updates showing contracted capacity moving into operating ARR and recognized AI revenue would directly test the transition thesis. The August 27 update reported $4 billion of contracted ARR and $1 billion operating at that time.

Further disclosure on GPU deployment, operating capacity, and delivery under customer contracts would clarify whether power and infrastructure arrangements are becoming productive capacity. No specific future event date is supplied.
Conversion of late-stage 2027 customer discussions into signed agreements could improve forward capacity visibility; the supplied announcement does not quantify timing or conversion likelihood.

runs.summary: IREN’s thesis depends on converting its capital-intensive Bitcoin-mining business into a larger AI cloud platform. Company-reported contracts and capacity plans support a demand case, while FY2026 losses, heavy capital spending, and a large gap between contracted and operating ARR leave execution and financing central. The September 28 close showed pronounced weakness relative to broad equity proxies. The evidence supports a high-uncertainty research view, not a settled conclusion.

keyFindings.text: Observed fact: IREN’s FY2026 10-K describes a vertically integrated AI cloud platform spanning data centers, compute, and software. For the year ended June 30, 2026, revenue was $707.0 million: $128.8 million from AI Cloud Services and $578.2 million from Bitcoin mining. AI remained a minority of reported revenue.

Issuer claim: In its August 27, 2026 results announcement, IREN reported $4 billion of contracted ARR for 2026 capacity, $1 billion of ARR operating at that time, and 2026 capacity largely sold out. These run-rate figures are not recognized FY2026 revenue; delivery and conversion remain important tests.

Issuer claim: The August results announcement described a new multi-year contract with a leading frontier AI lab, additional customer signings, and late-stage discussions over a significant portion of 2027 capacity. It does not quantify customer revenue shares or specify when those discussions would become signed contracts.

Observed fact: FY2026 revenue grew 41.1% year over year, while operating income was negative $1.05 billion, net income attributable to the parent was negative $702.6 million, and diluted EPS was negative $2.22. The supplied free-cash-flow proxy was negative $897.6 million; capex was $3.00 billion.

Observed fact: At June 30, 2026, cash was $5.90 billion, debt was $7.59 billion, and net debt was $1.70 billion. IREN reported $2.8 billion of GPU financing covering 90% of associated GPU capex. The financing helps fund expansion but does not remove broader capital and delivery risks.

risks.text: Observed fact: The latest supplied reported financial period ended June 30, 2026, nearly three months before this analysis. The evidence flags the reporting surface as not current for quarterly cadence, limiting visibility into present deployment, liquidity, and leverage.

Missing required source: The supplied 10-K evidence does not quantify customer concentration, revenue shares by customer or region, contract commencement schedules, renewal rates, or repeat-purchase rates. Those omissions limit assessment of diversification and contracted revenue quality.

Missing required source: SEC-derived company facts omit gross profit and comparable year-over-year debt figures; untagged interim facts were not validated. This limits analysis of unit economics and leverage trends.

Observed fact: The supplied balance sheet showed $7.59 billion of debt against $5.90 billion of cash at June 30, 2026, while FY2026 capex was $3.00 billion. GPU financing covers associated GPU capex as reported by the company, but total funding and execution risk remains.

Missing required source: No intraday, order-flow, short-interest, positioning, or current peer price and volume series is supplied. The September 28 price move cannot be decomposed into market, sector, and issuer effects.

catalysts.text: Issuer claim: Evidence of progress moving contracted capacity into operating ARR and recognized revenue would directly test the transition thesis; IREN reported $4 billion of contracted ARR and $1 billion operating at the time of its August 27 update.

Issuer claim: Conversion of late-stage 2027 customer discussions into signed agreements, alongside delivery under the new multi-year contract and recent signings, could strengthen forward capacity visibility.

Model inference: Updates on GPU deployment, operating capacity, and financing could clarify whether capital spending is translating into productive AI infrastructure; the supplied evidence gives no specific future event date.

Conflicting evidence: Recent coverage describes a sector-wide neocloud selloff alongside reports of rising GPU rental rates and analyst disagreement. Further sector pricing and demand evidence could alter the context for IREN’s capacity economics, but the reports are secondary.
